source-fm.title: fm: FM
source-fm.description: Phase-modulation (DX7-style FM) with up to 4 sine operators. Reach for it for bells, gongs, tubular chimes, metallic hits, electric zaps, FM brass and alien tones: anything bright whose overtones should move. Inharmonic ratios (3.5, 1.41, 2.76) ring like metal; whole-number ratios sound like instruments. A decaying modulator index makes a strike that mellows; a rising one, a swell. Softer events (vel < 1) are darker as well as quieter. High notes with big indices render at twice the rate, and the index only gives way where its sidebands would still alias, so nothing folds back.

algorithm.description: How the operators connect; ops[0] is always heard. stack: each operator modulates the one before it (ops[3] > ops[2] > ops[1] > ops[0]), the brightest and most complex. parallel: all the others modulate ops[0], a rich single tone. pairs: ops[1] modulates ops[0] and ops[3] modulates ops[2], two tones heard together (a bell's strike and hum, layered brass); with 3 operators ops[2] is a plain second carrier.

ops.description: The operators, 1 to 4 sine oscillators: `[{ "ratio": 1 }, { "ratio": 3.5, "index": 4, "env": { "decay": 0.8 } }]`. A modulator's `index` and `env` shape the brightness; a carrier's `level` and `env` its loudness.

items.description: One operator: { ratio or fixed, detune, index, env, feedback, level, id }.

ratio.description: Frequency as a multiple of `freq`. Whole numbers (1, 2, 3) give harmonic, musical tones; others (1.41, 2.76, 3.5) give inharmonic bells, gongs and clangs. Breakpoints sweep the sidebands: a sci-fi "bwow". (0.25 to 16x, log scale)

fixed.description: A fixed frequency instead of `ratio`; the operator then ignores the note and `pitch` (DX7 fixed mode). A slow fixed modulator (5 to 40 Hz) with a high index warbles or growls; a high one keeps the same clang under any note. (1 to 8000 Hz, log scale)

detune.description: Fine offset in cents. 2 to 8 cents on a second carrier makes slow beating; on a modulator the timbre shimmers. (-50 to 50 cents)

index.description: How hard this operator modulates its target, as peak phase deviation in radians (ignored on carriers). 0 is a pure sine, 1 to 2 warm, 3 to 6 bright and brassy, 8 to 15 metallic, 20+ noisy. Make it fall over time (breakpoints or `env`) for a struck sound that mellows. (0 to 15)

env.description: Envelope on this operator. On a modulator it scales `index`: `{ "decay": 0.6, "sustain": 0.1 }` starts bright and mellows like a bell, `{ "attack": 0.08, "sustain": 1 }` swells like brass. On a carrier it scales `level`. Default: constant.

feedback.description: The operator modulates itself: 0 is a sine, 0.5 adds harmonics, 1 is close to a sawtooth (buzzy, brassy), 1.5 and up breaks into noise. Lowered automatically at high pitch so it never aliases. (0 to 1.5)

level.description: Output level of a carrier, 0 to 1 (with two carriers, their balance); ignored on modulators. (0 to 1)

source-additive.title: additive: Additive
source-additive.description: Sums of sine partials, each with its own level and decay. Use the harmonic series (`harmonics`, `tilt`, `odd`, `stretch`) for beeps, UI tones, organ and flute-like tones and drones, or explicit `partials` for chimes, glass, bars and bells with measured ratios. `decay` with `damping` makes the highs die first, the signature of a real struck object; `beat` adds the slow shimmer of a bell. When the partials decay on their own, leave the envelope without a decay (the default) so they ring out.

damping.description: How much faster higher partials die: a partial's decay is `decay` / ratio^damping. 0 all ring equally (glass, an organ), 1 natural for struck wood and metal, 2 dull and woody. (0 to 3)

beat.description: Doubles each partial a few cents apart so it beats slowly like a real bell or glass: 2 to 6 cents shimmer, 15+ a chorus. 0 is off. (0 to 20 cents)

width.description: Stereo spread: each partial gets its own place, 0 (mono) to 1 (wide). Stereo output only. (0 to 1)

source-voice.title: voice: Voice
source-voice.description: A throat: shaped glottal pulses at `freq` (with natural `jitter` and `shimmer`) and `breath`, through formants that morph between vowels and scale with `size`. Reach for it for creatures, monsters, robots, grunts, moans, critter squeaks and whispers: anything with a throat. `growl` adds a clean subharmonic snarl, `rasp` a torn hoarseness, `tension` goes from a sigh to a strained shout. Pitch and vowel curves are what make it emote: a rising then falling `freq` with `vowel` moving from 0 to 3 is a roar.

size.description: Size of the throat: divides every formant frequency. 0.5 a tiny critter or a child, 1 an adult, 2 a big beast, 3+ a kaiju. Independent of pitch, so a small high voice or a huge low one are both easy. (0.3 to 4x, log scale)

tension.description: How pressed the vocal folds are: 0 soft and dull (a sigh, a moan), 0.5 normal, 1 pressed and buzzy (a strained shout, a robot). Louder events (vel) press a little harder. (0 to 1)

breath.description: Aspiration noise through the same throat: 0 clean, 0.2 natural, 0.5 husky, 1 a whisper with no tone left. (0 to 1)

jitter.description: Random cycle-to-cycle pitch wobble, percent: 0 mechanical (a robot), 0.5 to 1.5 alive, 4 to 10 rough and old. (0 to 10 %)

shimmer.description: Random cycle-to-cycle level wobble, dB: 0 steady, 0.5 to 1 natural, 3 to 6 shaky and broken. (0 to 6 dB)

growl.description: Subharmonic roughness: every other pulse weakens and shifts (period doubling), adding a tone an octave down while the harmonics stay clean. 0.3 gruff, 0.6 a monster growl, 1 a deep snarl an octave below `freq`. (0 to 1)

rasp.description: Noisy, irregular roughness (a torn, hoarse throat): fast random flutter of the pulses. 0.3 hoarse, 0.7 a snarling hiss-roar, 1 shredded. (0 to 1)

source-machine.title: machine: Machine
source-machine.description: Rotating machinery driven by `rpm`: pick the `kind` (motor, servo, drill, engine, turbine, rotor) and move `rpm` with breakpoints so it spins up, holds, strains and winds down; every tone, pulse and chop follows it. `load` is the strain (rougher, brighter, louder), `roughness` how uneven it is, `whine` its gear whine. For a helicopter, layer the main rotor with a second, small, fast rotor for the tail (4 blades, about 1000 rpm, size 0.4) and a quiet turbine; for a car pass-by, put an engine through doppler.

Typical: motor 1000 to 6000 (hum at rpm/30 Hz), servo 4000 to 15000, drill 8000 to 30000, engine 700 idle to 7000 redline, turbine 2000 to 15000, rotor 250 to 400 (helicopter) or 600 to 2000 (fan). cylinders.description: Engine only: 1 thumps like a dirt bike or lawnmower, 2 a twin, 4 a car, 6 smooth, 8 a V8 rumble. Fires cylinders * rpm / 120 times a second, each cylinder a little different. (1 to 12)

blades.description: Rotor: blades per revolution, slapping blades * rpm / 60 times a second (2 a helicopter, 4 to 7 a fan). Turbine: fan blades, setting the whine at blades * rpm / 60 Hz (default 22). (2 to 40)

size.description: Size of the machine: lowers its body, pipe and air resonances. 0.4 a toy or a model, 1 normal, 2 a truck, a ship's engine or a heavy-lift helicopter. (0.3 to 3x, log scale)

source-chaos.title: chaos: Chaos
source-chaos.description: Nonlinear and digital generators: maps and attractors on the edge of chaos, cross-modulated sines and bytebeat formulas. Reach for it for glitches, data noise, broken or alien electronics, malfunctioning robots, sci-fi computers and creature textures: sounds that are structured but never quite repeat. `chaos` moves it from a stable tone into noise; `rate` is its speed or pitch; `smooth` takes the digital edge off. The seed sets the starting point, so every take differs.

Default per mode: 3000, 3000, 220, 220, 8000. (20 to 20000 Hz, log scale, follows pitch)

smooth.description: Output smoothing, 0 to 1: 0 raw stepped digital grit, 0.5 softened, 1 smooth and dark (maps and bytebeat: interpolated and low-passed at half the rate; lorenz and feedback: only the lowest harmonics left). (0 to 1)

ratio.description: feedback only: frequency of the second oscillator as a multiple of `rate`. 1 or 2 locks into buzzy tones, 1.41 or 2.76 grinds. (0.25 to 8x, log scale)

formula.description: bytebeat only: the formula. sierpinski: a fractal arpeggio. melody: a chiptune tune. glitch: busy, broken rhythms. techno: a sequenced loop. harmony: chords that shift. bitshift: data noise and squeals. crush: collapsing, grinding bits.

source-modal.title: modal: Modal object
source-modal.description: A resonant solid object, described by what it is: a `material` (how it loses its ring), a `shape` (which modes it has), a size (`freq`) and what sets it off (`exciter`: a strike, a noisy hit, a scrape or a roll). Reach for it for anything hit, dropped, knocked, clinked, dragged or rolled: pans, bottles, planks, bells, drums, coins, doors, pipes, rocks. It replaces the usual "sine thump plus a few decaying partials" with the real mode pattern of the object, so a metal bar, a wine glass and a wooden box differ the way they do in life. Make it broken with `dent`, shimmering with `beat`, held or wet with `damping`; change `position` and `exciter.hardness` for a different hit on the same thing. The ring is the envelope: leave `env` alone and set `decay`. An event's `dur` damps it like a hand.

material.description: What it is made of: sets how fast high modes die and the default `decay`. metal rings long and bright (2.5 s), glass clear (1.2 s), ceramic a shorter clink (0.6 s), stone a hard click (0.14 s), wood a warm knock (0.25 s), plastic a dull tap (0.12 s), skin a drum head (0.5 s), rubber and cardboard dead thumps (0.08 s).

shape.description: What the object is, which sets the spacing of its modes. bar: a free bar or rod, wide inharmonic gaps (1, 2.76, 5.4: chimes, xylophone, pipe, wrench). tine: a bar held at one end (1, 6.27, 17.5: a thin ping with a high clang: fork, tongue, ruler). plate: a sheet, dense clangour (sheet metal, pan lid, sign, glass pane). membrane: a stretched skin (drums; struck in the centre it is a pitchless thud). bell: church-bell partials with the minor third; `freq` is the hum, the heard note is an octave above. bowl: rim modes (1, 2.83, 5.4: wine glass, cup, bowl, hoop). tube: the air in a pipe, odd harmonics (hollow: bottle, bamboo, slapped pipe). string: harmonics (wire, cable, spring; a tonal clang). box: an enclosed cavity, crowded low modes (crate, cabinet, drawer, body thump). random: an irregular lump with its own modes for each `variant` (rock, junk, debris).

freq.description: Frequency of the lowest mode: the size of the object. 60 to 150 a drum, tank or door; 200 to 600 a pan, bottle or plank; 800 to 3000 a glass, key or coin; above that tiny things. Breakpoints bend every mode together (a wobbling sheet, a filling glass). (30 to 8000 Hz, log scale, follows pitch)

decay.description: Seconds for the lowest mode to fall 60 dB. Left out, the material chooses (see `material`). Shorter is a damped, held or lying object; longer one hanging free. (0.02 to 8 s, log scale)

damping.description: How much faster high modes die than the lowest, times the material's own loss: 0 all ring equally long (unnaturally pure), 1 the material itself, 2 to 4 a damp, cracked, wet or hand-held object whose ring dulls at once. (0 to 4x)

brightness.description: Tilt of the mode levels: 0.5 is the material's own balance, 0 leaves little but the lowest mode (dark, heavy, thick), 1 makes high modes as loud as low ones (thin, splashy, brittle). (0 to 1)

modes.description: How many modes ring. 4 to 8 is a simple, pure object; 16 to 32 a realistic one; 48+ dense clangour (plates, crashes). (1 to 64)

stretch.description: Bends the spacing of the modes: each ratio is raised to this power. 1 is the shape's physics; below 1 crowds the modes together (thicker, heavier, more clustered); above 1 spreads them (thinner, glassier). On `string` 1.02 to 1.1 is a stiff wire, like a piano's. (0.6 to 1.5)

dent.description: Damage: detunes each mode at random and unevens their levels and decays. 0 a perfect object, 0.1 to 0.3 hand-made or worn, 0.5 to 1 dented, cracked, bent junk. `variant` picks the pattern. (0 to 1)

position.description: Where it is struck: 0 the centre (few modes, round and hollow), 1 the edge or end (every mode, bright and clangy). For `tine` 0 is the held end and 1 the tip; for `box` 0 is the middle and 1 a corner. (0 to 1)

beat.description: Splits every mode into a detuned pair that beats, as in bells, gongs, bowls and anything not quite round. Hz of the slowest wobble: 0 off, 0.5 to 3 a slow shimmer, 5 to 15 a fast flutter, 30+ rough. (0 to 20 Hz)

variant.description: Which object: picks the `dent` pattern and the modes of the `random` shape. The same number is the same object in every event and every take, so repeats sound like one thing being hit again. (1 to 99)

exciter.description: What sets it ringing: { kind, hardness, duration, density, roughness }.

kind.description: What sets the object ringing. impulse: an ideal click that drives every mode (the brightest, cleanest strike). mallet: a blow with a contact time set by `hardness` (felt to steel). noise: a rough, crumbling hit that fades over `duration`. scrape: dragged across ridges or grit for `duration` (`density` ridges per second, `roughness` regular comb to random grit). roll: rolling or rattling for `duration` (`density` bumps per second, with the wobble of a turning object).

hardness.description: How hard the contact is: 0 a soft felt or rubber beater (long contact, only the lowest modes: a thud or a pure boom), 0.5 wood or a knuckle, 1 steel on steel (every mode: a bright clank). For noise, scrape and roll it is the brightness of the friction. Louder events (`vel`) hit a little harder. (0 to 1)

duration.description: Seconds the noise fades over, or the scrape or roll lasts. The ring follows it. Ignored by impulse and mallet. (0.01 to 4 s, log scale)

density.description: Ridges (scrape) or bumps (roll) per second: the speed of the motion. 20 to 80 is a slow ratchet or a heavy ball, 200 to 2000 a fast drag. Breakpoints speed it up or slow it to a stop. (5 to 3000 Hz, log scale)

roughness.description: Scrape: 0 evenly spaced ridges (a comb, a zip, a guiro: a buzzing pitch at `density`), 1 random grit with hiss. Roll: how uneven the bumps are and how much surface rumble there is. (0 to 1)

source-pluck.title: pluck: String
source-pluck.description: A vibrating string modelled as a travelling wave in a loop (a waveguide, the descendant of Karplus-Strong): every harmonic is there at the start and each fades at its own rate, which no stack of sine partials imitates. Reach for it for plucks, twangs, harp and koto notes, rubber bands, taut cables and fence wires, piano-like strikes (`excite: strike`, a little `stiffness`), muted thunks (`mute`), cartoon boings and springs (high `stiffness`, low `freq`, often with `freq` gliding), and scraped or bowed wires (`excite: bow`). The ring is the envelope: leave `env` alone and set `decay`.

gain.description: Level of this source in dB. (-48 to 12 dB)

env.description: Amplitude envelope: { attack, hold, decay, sustain, release, gate } in seconds, or { points: [[t, level], ...] }.

pitch.description: Semitones added to every pitched parameter. Breakpoints make a whole-voice pitch sweep. (-48 to 48 st)

filter.description: Per-voice filter, applied before the envelope, so every event gets its own sweep.

cutoff.description: Cutoff or centre frequency. (20 to 20000 Hz, log scale)

q.description: Resonance: 0.707 is flat, 2 to 10 rings. (0.3 to 20, log scale)

gain.description: dB, for peak and shelf types. (-24 to 24 dB)

keytrack.description: How much the cutoff follows pitch, 0 to 1. (0 to 1)

freq.description: Pitch of the string. 40 to 100 a bass string or a long cable, 110 to 660 guitar range, above 1000 short wires and pings. It may glide: breakpoints bend the ringing string (a dive, a whammy, a "boing" that drops). (30 to 4000 Hz, log scale, follows pitch)

decay.description: Seconds for the fundamental to fall 60 dB. 0.1 to 0.4 a damped or rubbery twang, 1 to 3 a guitar string, 5+ a long steel wire. High harmonics always die sooner (see `brightness`). (0.05 to 10 s, log scale)

brightness.description: How long the high harmonics last: 0 a dull thump that turns to a sine at once (gut, rubber band, felt), 0.5 nylon, 0.7 steel, 1 an endless bright wire (harpsichord, zing). It may move: sweep it down for a string being damped. (0 to 1)

position.description: Where along the string it is excited, as a fraction of its length: 0.5 the middle (round, hollow, odd harmonics only), 0.15 to 0.25 a normal pluck, 0.03 to 0.08 right at the bridge (thin, nasal, twangy). (0.02 to 0.5)

stiffness.description: How much the string is a rod: stiffness makes high harmonics travel faster, so they go sharp. 0 an ideal string, 0.2 to 0.45 piano and thick wound strings (the 14th harmonic up to 1 % sharp), 0.5 to 0.7 a stiff wire with a clangy edge, 0.8 to 1 a coil spring whose overtones run away (at 1: 1, 2.06, 3.2, 4.6, 6.4 times the pitch) and whose every trip round smears into a chirp: boing, sproing, spring-reverb twang. Best with `freq` below 150. (0 to 1)

excite.description: pluck: a pick or finger lets go (a burst as long as one period). strike: a hammer blow (piano, dulcimer, a cable hit with a wrench; rounder attack). bow: noisy friction drives the string for as long as the event is held (`dur`), or `bowTime` if it has none: an airy, singing, scraped tone that swells in.

hardness.description: Brightness of the attack: 0 the flesh of a thumb or a felt hammer, 0.6 a plectrum, 1 a metal edge. For bow, how gritty the friction is. Louder events (`vel`) dig in a little harder. (0 to 1)

mute.description: Damping by a hand on the string: 0 open, 0.3 to 0.6 palm mute (short, dull, percussive), 1 fully choked (a pitched thud). Breakpoints stop a ringing string: [[0, 0], [0.4, 0], [0.45, 1]]. (0 to 1)

bowTime.description: Seconds the bow stays on the string when the event has no `dur`. The string rings on for `decay` after it lifts. (0.05 to 5 s, log scale)

source-particles.title: particles: Particles
source-particles.description: A cloud of tiny separate sounds, each with its own pitch, level and ring: what filtered noise can only smear. Reach for it whenever a sound is really many small things: gravel and debris after an impact (`burst`), rain and hail (`random` ticks or drops), fire and frying (crackle), sparks (chirp), spilled coins or broken glass (modal grains), bubbles and pouring (drop), a Geiger counter or ratchet (click), a coin or ball bouncing to rest (`bounce`), or a shimmering granular cloud (grain). Describe the pieces in `grain` (how they sound, the range of their sizes) and how they fall with `density`, `duration` and `distribution`. The common `pitch` parameter shifts the whole range and may move. Layer it after a modal or noise impact for the aftermath.

gain.description: Level of this source in dB. (-48 to 12 dB)

env.description: Amplitude envelope: { attack, hold, decay, sustain, release, gate } in seconds, or { points: [[t, level], ...] }.

pitch.description: Semitones added to every pitched parameter. Breakpoints make a whole-voice pitch sweep. (-48 to 48 st)

filter.description: Per-voice filter, applied before the envelope, so every event gets its own sweep.

cutoff.description: Cutoff or centre frequency. (20 to 20000 Hz, log scale)

q.description: Resonance: 0.707 is flat, 2 to 10 rings. (0.3 to 20, log scale)

gain.description: dB, for peak and shelf types. (-24 to 24 dB)

keytrack.description: How much the cutoff follows pitch, 0 to 1. (0 to 1)

density.description: Particles per second. 2 to 10 scattered drips and clicks, 20 to 100 a patter, 200 to 1000 a shower or sizzle, 3000+ a hiss. Breakpoints over the event build or thin it: [[0, 5], [2, 400]] is rain setting in. For burst it is the rate at the first instant and thins as exp(-5 t / duration), so a burst emits about density x duration / 5 grains. Ignored by bounce. (0.5 to 2000 Hz, log scale)

duration.description: Seconds over which particles are emitted (an event's `dur` ends it sooner). The last ones ring past it. (0.05 to 10 s, log scale)

distribution.description: How particles fall in time. random: independent, like rain or a Geiger counter. regular: evenly spaced, loosened by `jitter` (ratchet, gear, card in spokes, dripping tap). burst: densest at the first instant and thinning to nothing by the end, the pieces getting quieter (debris after an impact, a spill, a shatter). bounce: one object bouncing to rest, each gap `ratio` times the last, starting at `interval` (ball, coin, dropped lid; every bounce is the same piece, softer each time).

jitter.description: Irregularity of regular spacing (0 a machine, 0.3 a hand, 1 nearly random) and of bounce gaps (a wobbling, spinning coin). (0 to 1)

interval.description: Bounce: seconds between the first and second impact. 0.5 a ball from waist height, 0.15 a coin or bottle cap from a few centimetres. (0.02 to 1.5 s, log scale)

ratio.description: Bounce: each gap is the last times this. 0.5 a dead thing that stops in a few hops, 0.75 a hard ball, 0.9 a ping-pong ball rattling to a buzz. (0.3 to 0.95)

spread.description: Stereo scatter: 0 mono, 1 each particle anywhere between hard left and hard right (stereo output only). (0 to 1)

grain.description: One particle: { kind, lo, hi, decayLo, decayHi, levelJitter, pitchJitter, size, material, shape, tone, sweep }.

kind.description: What one particle sounds like. tick: a tiny burst of noise around its frequency (gravel, sand, rain on leaves, hail, rustle). click: a bare broadband click, brighter with frequency (Geiger counter, relay, vinyl, static, ratchet). ping: a small pure ring (glass dust, tinkles, droplets on metal). drop: a water drop or bubble, a ring whose pitch rises (rain on water, pouring, boiling, fizz). chirp: a quick sweep by `sweep` octaves (sparks, zaps, birds, insects). crackle: a sharp pop with a ragged tail and wildly uneven levels (fire, embers, frying, ice, static). modal: a small struck object of `material` and `shape` (coins, shards, pebbles, nails, wood chips, shells). grain: a smooth window of tone or noise (`tone`) for granular clouds, shimmer and swarms.

lo.description: Lowest frequency a particle may have; each draws its own between `lo` and `hi`, evenly by ratio. The pair is the size range of the pieces. Breakpoints move the range over the event (bubbles rising, debris getting finer). (40 to 12000 Hz, log scale, follows pitch)

hi.description: Highest frequency a particle may have. Equal to `lo`, every particle has the same pitch. (40 to 16000 Hz, log scale, follows pitch)

decayLo.description: Shortest ring of a particle (seconds to fall 60 dB; for `grain` the length of the window). 0.002 to 0.01 dry ticks, 0.03 to 0.15 small ringing things, 0.3+ glass and metal. Ignored by click. (0.001 to 1 s, log scale)

decayHi.description: Longest ring of a particle, seconds. (0.001 to 2 s, log scale)

levelJitter.description: How far below full level a particle may be, dB: 0 all equal (mechanical), 12 natural, 30 a few loud ones over a quiet bed. (0 to 40 dB)

pitchJitter.description: Random detune of each particle on top of its place in the range, semitones. With `lo` = `hi` or `bounce` it is the only pitch variation. (0 to 12 st)

size.description: Ties pitch, level and ring together as size does: at 1 the low particles are the loud, long-ringing ones (big pieces) and the high ones faint and short; at 0 the three vary independently. (0 to 1)

material.description: For kind modal: what the pieces are made of (see the modal source).

shape.description: For kind modal: the shape of the pieces. plate for shards and coins, bar for nails and sticks, random for rubble.

tone.description: For kind grain: 0 a puff of band noise, 1 a pure tone, between a breathy tone. (0 to 1)

sweep.description: For kind chirp: octaves the pitch moves over the particle. -2 a falling zap or spark, +1 a rising blip or chirrup. (-4 to 4)

effect-filter.title: filter: Filter
effect-filter.description: Resonant state-variable filter over the whole track (or bus/master). Use the voice `filter` instead when each event needs its own sweep. Breakpoints on `cutoff` are measured from the start of the track.

cutoff.description: Cutoff or centre frequency. (20 to 20000 Hz, log scale)

q.description: Resonance: 0.707 flat, 2 to 10 rings. (0.3 to 20, log scale)

gain.description: dB for peak and shelf types. (-24 to 24 dB)

effect-drive.title: drive: Drive
effect-drive.description: Saturation and distortion, oversampled. tanh is warm tape-like saturation, soft is gentle, hard is digital clipping, fold is a wavefolder (bright and metallic), tube adds even harmonics, fuzz is broken-transistor grit, rectify jumps the pitch up an octave and sounds ring-modulated. `amount` is the gain into the shaper; the output is matched to the input peak unless `compensate` is off.

amount.description: Gain into the shaper, dB. 6 is warm, 18 is crunchy, 30+ is destroyed. (0 to 48 dB)

bias.description: Asymmetry, -1 to 1: adds even harmonics and a sputtering edge. (-1 to 1)

tone.description: Low-pass after the shaper, Hz: tames fizz. (500 to 20000 Hz, log scale)

output.description: Level after the shaper, dB. (-24 to 12 dB)

compensate.description: Match the output peak to the input peak.

oversample.description: Oversampling: more is cleaner and slower.

effect-gain.title: gain: Gain
effect-gain.description: Level over time in dB: draw swells, fades and ducks with breakpoints measured from the start of the track (a riser that swells for 1.5 s and cuts: [[0, -30], [1.5, 0], [1.52, -90]]). `invert` flips polarity.

gain.description: Level, dB. (-60 to 24 dB)

effect-eq.title: eq: EQ
effect-eq.description: Parametric EQ: up to 8 bands in series, each a lowcut, highcut, lowshelf, highshelf, peak or notch. Reach for it to fit a layer into the mix (cut the lows a layer does not need so the layers stop muddying each other), to shape tone (a presence peak for bite, a high shelf for air, a highcut for distance) or to remove a whistle with a notch. Every band's freq, gain and q can move over time. For one resonant sweep use `filter`.

bands.description: The bands, applied in order (8 at most; more are ignored): [{ "mode": "lowcut", "freq": 120, "slope": "24" }, { "mode": "peak", "freq": 3000, "gain": 4, "q": 1.2 }, { "mode": "highshelf", "freq": 9000, "gain": -6 }]. Give a band an `id` to reach it by name from controls.

items.description: One band: { mode, freq, gain, q, slope }.

id.description: Name for paths and controls, e.g. `tracks.x.fx.eq.bands.air.gain` for the band `"id": "air"`.

mode.description: Band shape. lowcut removes everything below `freq` (rumble, mud; `slope` sets how steep), highcut everything above (fizz, hiss: a darker, farther sound). lowshelf and highshelf tilt everything below or above `freq` by `gain` (weight, air). peak boosts or cuts a bell around `freq` (presence at 2 to 5 kHz, boxiness at 300 to 600 Hz). notch removes a narrow band (a whistle, a hum).

freq.description: Corner or centre frequency. 30 to 80 Hz sub and rumble, 100 to 250 body, 300 to 600 box and mud, 1 to 4 kHz presence and bite, 5 to 10 kHz sizzle, 10 to 16 kHz air. Breakpoints sweep it from the start of the buffer. (20 to 20000 Hz, log scale)

gain.description: Boost (+) or cut (-) for peak and shelf bands, dB. ±3 is a nudge, ±6 clear, ±12 drastic. Cuts and notches ignore it. (-24 to 24 dB)

q.description: Width or resonance. peak: 0.5 broad and gentle, 0.7 musical (default), 2 to 5 narrow, 10+ surgical. notch: 2 to 10 (higher is narrower). Cuts and shelves: 0.707 is flat; 1.5 to 4 adds a resonant bump at the corner (a cut that rings like an analog synth filter). Ignored by 6 dB cuts. (0.3 to 20, log scale)

slope.description: Steepness of lowcut and highcut, dB per octave: 6 gentle, 12 (default) and 24 clean, 36 and 48 a brick wall.

bypass.description: Skip this band (for comparing with and without).

output.description: Level after the EQ, dB: make up for big cuts or boosts. (-24 to 24 dB)

effect-compressor.title: compressor: Compressor
effect-compressor.description: Turns the loud parts down by `ratio` above `threshold`. Reach for it to make a hit punchier (attack 0.01 to 0.03 s lets the crack through, then clamps the body; add `autoMakeup` and the hit stands out), to glue layers on a bus (ratio 2, threshold -10, attack 0.02, release 0.2: they move as one), or to bring up a tail (fast attack, high ratio: the ring and room come forward). By default the threshold is measured from the loudest moment of its input (`reference: "peak"`), so it acts the same whatever the layer's level.

threshold.description: Level above which the gain comes down, dB below the loudest moment of the input (or dBFS with `reference: "dbfs"`). -6 touches only the peaks, -12 to -20 works the body, -30 and below squashes everything. (-48 to 0 dB)

ratio.description: dB in for each dB out above the threshold. 1.5 to 2 gentle glue, 3 to 4 firm and punchy, 8+ squashed, 20+ a limiter. (1 to 20x, log scale)

attack.description: Time constant for the gain to come down. 0.0005 to 0.003 catches the transient (flatter, smoother), 0.01 to 0.03 lets the crack through before clamping (punchier), 0.05+ barely touches short hits. (0.0002 to 0.1 s, log scale)

release.description: Time constant for the gain to recover. 0.05 to 0.1 lively (can pump on dense sounds), 0.15 to 0.3 smooth glue, 0.5+ slow and steady. Short releases bring tails and room up between hits. (0.02 to 1 s, log scale)

knee.description: Width of the soft knee around the threshold, dB: 0 hard and obvious, 6 natural, 12+ very gradual. (0 to 24 dB)

makeup.description: Gain after compression, dB (added to `autoMakeup`). (-12 to 24 dB)

autoMakeup.description: Raise the output to the loudness (rms) of the input, so the layer keeps its place in the mix and only its dynamics change.

detector.description: peak reacts to every peak (tight control, catches clicks); rms follows the average level over about 10 ms (smoother, lets fast transients slip through: punchier).

lookahead.description: Seconds the detector sees ahead, so the gain is already down when a peak arrives (no latency offline). 0 keeps the punch; 0.001 to 0.005 catches it cleanly. (0 to 0.01 s, log scale)

link.description: Stereo link, 0 to 1: 1 one gain for both channels (the image stays put), 0 each channel on its own. (0 to 1)

reference.description: What `threshold` is measured from: peak (the loudest moment of this input: predictable at any level) or dbfs (absolute, like a hardware unit).

effect-limiter.title: limiter: Limiter
effect-limiter.description: Brickwall peak limiter with lookahead: no sample ever goes over `ceiling`. Push `gain` into it to make a sound denser and louder (6 dB is firm, 12 dB squashed and loud, 18+ crushed). By default levels are measured from the input's own peak (`reference: "peak"`), so `{ "gain": 6 }` always takes 6 dB off the peaks and raises everything else by 6 dB, whatever the layer's level. Use `reference: "dbfs"` for an absolute safety ceiling, with the master's `normalize` set to none.

gain.description: Input gain into the limiter, dB: the dB the peaks are pushed past the ceiling. 3 to 6 firm, 9 to 12 loud and dense, 18+ crushed. Breakpoints push harder over time. (0 to 24 dB)

ceiling.description: Highest level the output may reach, dB relative to the input's peak (or dBFS with `reference: "dbfs"`, where -1 leaves room for export). (-24 to 0 dB)

release.description: Time constant for the gain to recover after a peak. 0.01 to 0.03 loud but gritty on low notes, 0.05 to 0.1 clean, 0.3+ smooth and slow. (0.005 to 1 s, log scale)

lookahead.description: Seconds the gain starts coming down before a peak (no latency offline): the length of the gain ramp. 0.001 snappy, 0.003 clean, 0.01 smoothest. (0.0005 to 0.01 s, log scale)

reference.description: What `ceiling` is measured from: peak (the input's own loudest sample) or dbfs (absolute full scale).

effect-transient.title: transient: Transient shaper
effect-transient.description: Shapes the attack and the body of a sound independently of its level, from the difference of fast and slow envelope followers. The key tool for punch: `attack` +6 to +12 makes a hit snap and cut through, -6 to -12 softens a click into a thud; `sustain` +6 rings out longer and brings up the room, -6 to -18 tightens a boomy hit until it is dry and short. Works on single hits, rolls and whole buses alike.

attack.description: dB added at each onset, fading over `window`. +6 snappier, +12 a hard crack; negative softens the hit. (-24 to 24 dB)

sustain.description: dB added to the body: what follows each onset, more as it decays. + rings longer and fuller, - tighter and drier. (-24 to 24 dB)

window.description: Seconds the onset emphasis lasts: 0.003 to 0.008 just the click, 0.015 to 0.03 a drum hit (default 0.02), 0.05+ a slow boom. (0.002 to 0.1 s, log scale)

effect-gate.title: gate: Gate
effect-gate.description: Closes when the sound falls below `threshold`, turning it down by `range`. Reach for it to chop a tail short (a gated boom, a dry hit from a ringing one), to cut the noise between hits, or for stutters on a rolling sound. By default the threshold is measured from the input's loudest moment (`reference: "peak"`): -20 keeps only the loud part of a hit, -40 trims the very end of a tail. A shallow `range` (-6 to -12) is a gentle expander that just pushes tails down.

threshold.description: Level at which the gate opens, dB below the input's loudest moment (or dBFS with `reference: "dbfs"`). -10 to -20 chops hard, -30 to -50 trims tails. (-80 to 0 dB)

range.description: How far the closed gate turns the sound down, dB: -80 silence, -20 a clear dip, -6 a gentle expander. (-90 to 0 dB)

attack.description: Seconds to open fully. 0.0002 to 0.001 keeps the crack of a hit; 0.005 to 0.02 fades notes in softly. (0.0001 to 0.05 s, log scale)

hold.description: Seconds the gate stays open after the sound drops below the threshold: stops it fluttering on a decaying note. 0.01 to 0.05. (0 to 0.5 s, log scale)

release.description: Seconds to close (to fall 60 dB, or to `range` if that is shallower). 0.01 to 0.03 a hard chop, 0.1 to 0.3 a natural fade. (0.005 to 1 s, log scale)

lookahead.description: Seconds the gate sees ahead, so it is already open when a hit arrives and the attack is never clipped (no latency offline). (0 to 0.01 s, log scale)

hysteresis.description: dB below the threshold the level must fall before the gate closes again: stops chatter around the threshold. (0 to 12 dB)

reference.description: What `threshold` is measured from: peak (the input's loudest moment) or dbfs (absolute).

effect-crush.title: crush: Bitcrusher
effect-crush.description: Lo-fi grit: fewer bits (a coarse, noisy staircase, measured from the input's own peak so the same `bits` sound the same at any level) and a lower sample rate (sample and hold: metallic aliasing). Chiptune: bits 4, rate 8000. Old sampler: bits 12, rate 22050, antialias. Broken radio or a dying robot: bits 3, rate 3000, jitter 0.5. Sweep `bits` or `rate` with breakpoints for a sound that degrades or powers down.

bits.description: Bit depth, fractions allowed. 12 to 16 subtle hiss on quiet parts, 8 gritty, 4 to 6 chiptune crunch, 1 to 3 a buzzing, broken square. (1 to 16)

rate.description: Sample rate the sound is held at, Hz: 22050 dull and a little crunchy, 8000 to 11025 chiptune and old games, 2000 to 4000 a buzzing wreck. 48000 or more (or the output rate) leaves the rate alone. (500 to 48000 Hz, log scale)

jitter.description: Randomness of the sample clock, 0 to 1: a cheap, unstable converter. 0.1 grainy, 0.5 noisy and broken. (0 to 1)

antialias.description: Low-pass before and after the rate reduction, like a real sampler: darker and cleaner, without the metallic aliasing.

effect-tremolo.title: tremolo: Tremolo
effect-tremolo.description: Level wobble from an LFO: shimmer and pulse (sine, 4 to 8 Hz), throb (sine, 1 to 3 Hz), helicopter or rotor chop (square, 10 to 25 Hz), stutter and glitch (square or random, depth 1), alarm pulses. In stereo, `stereo: 0.5` swings the sound between left and right (auto-pan). Above about 30 Hz it turns into a rough, buzzing amplitude modulation. `rate` can move: a rotor spinning up is [[0, 4], [1.5, 22]].

rate.description: LFO speed, Hz. 0.5 to 3 slow throb, 4 to 8 classic tremolo, 10 to 25 chop and flutter, 30+ buzzing. (0.1 to 40 Hz, log scale)

depth.description: How deep the dips go, 0 to 1: 0.2 a subtle shimmer, 0.5 clear, 1 down to silence (a chop with square). (0 to 1)

shape.description: LFO shape: sine smooth, triangle even, square on-off chop, saw a pulse that fades, ramp one that swells, random a new level each cycle (flicker).

phase.description: Where in the cycle it starts, 0 to 1. Sine and triangle: 0 halfway and rising, 0.25 full level, 0.75 the deepest dip. Square and saw start at full level, ramp at the dip; 0.5 flips them. (0 to 1)

stereo.description: Phase offset of the right channel in cycles (stereo output only): 0 both pulse together, 0.5 they alternate (auto-pan), 0.25 a circling motion. (0 to 1)

effect-ringmod.title: ringmod: Ring modulator
effect-ringmod.description: Multiplies the sound by a carrier wave: every frequency in the input is replaced by its sum and difference with the carrier, which is inharmonic and metallic. Robot and dalek voices: sine at 30 to 80 Hz. Metallic, bell-like and alien tones from anything: 300 to 1500 Hz. Sci-fi radio: square carrier. `bias` keeps some of the original (amplitude modulation). Sweep `freq` for a sound that bends strangely.

freq.description: Carrier frequency, Hz. 20 to 80 a robotic buzz, 100 to 400 a growling metal ring, 500 to 2000 bells and clangs, 2000+ a thin, whistling shimmer. (10 to 5000 Hz, log scale)

shape.description: Carrier wave: sine the cleanest (two sidebands), triangle a little richer, square and saw harsh and buzzy (many sidebands).

bias.description: Keeps the original under the sidebands, 0 to 1: 0 pure ring modulation (the original pitch vanishes), 0.5 amplitude modulation, 1 no effect. (0 to 1)

effect-chorus.title: chorus: Chorus
effect-chorus.description: Copies of the sound, each slightly delayed and gently detuned by a slow wobble, mixed with the original: thicker, shimmering, ensemble-like. In stereo the copies are spread left and right, which widens a mono layer. Reach for it on pads, drones, magic shimmers, choirs and synth tones; with high `depth` and `rate` it turns seasick and warbly (a broken tape, an underwater feel). The output already contains the original; lower `mix` for a subtler effect.

rate.description: Wobble speed, Hz. 0.2 to 0.6 slow and lush, 0.8 to 1.5 classic, 3 to 8 a fast warble. (0.05 to 8 Hz, log scale)

depth.description: How far the delay swings, as a fraction of `delay`: 0.1 subtle, 0.25 rich (default), 0.5+ seasick detuning. (0 to 0.9)

delay.description: Average delay of the copies, seconds: 0.006 to 0.01 tight and bright, 0.012 to 0.02 classic, 0.03 doubling. (0.004 to 0.04 s, log scale)

voices.description: Delayed copies, 1 to 4: 1 is a simple chorus, 3 to 4 a dense ensemble. (1 to 4)

spread.description: Stereo spread of the copies, 0 to 1 (stereo output only): 0 the same in both ears, 1 opposite wobbles left and right (widest). (0 to 1)

effect-flanger.title: flanger: Flanger
effect-flanger.description: Mixes the sound with a copy delayed by a few milliseconds while the delay sweeps, so a comb of notches slides up and down: a swirling, whooshing sweep. Feedback sharpens the notches into ringing peaks: the jet plane (feedback 0.7 to 0.9, rate 0.1 to 0.3 on noise or a rumble), metallic robots and sci-fi doors (negative feedback is hollower). For one sweep instead of a cycle, set `depth: 0` and draw `delay` with breakpoints: [[0, 0.008], [2, 0.0003]] is a jet passing. The output already contains the original.

delay.description: Centre of the sweep, seconds: 0.001 bright and zingy, 0.003 classic, 0.008 lower and chorus-like. Breakpoints draw the sweep by hand. (0.0003 to 0.012 s, log scale)

depth.description: How far the LFO sweeps the delay either side of its centre, 0 to 1: 0.3 a gentle swirl, 0.7 classic, 0.95 near zero and back (the full jet). (0 to 1)

rate.description: Sweep speed, Hz: 0.05 to 0.3 slow jet, 0.5 to 2 swirling, 3+ wobbly. (0.02 to 5 Hz, log scale)

feedback.description: How much of the delayed sound goes round again, -0.95 to 0.95: 0 soft notches, 0.5 pronounced, 0.8+ resonant and metallic; negative is hollower. (-0.95 to 0.95)

shape.description: Sweep shape: triangle (even, classic) or sine (lingers at the ends).

stereo.description: Phase offset of the right channel's sweep in cycles (stereo output only): 0 the same, 0.25 swirling width, 0.5 opposite. (0 to 1)

effect-phaser.title: phaser: Phaser
effect-phaser.description: A chain of allpass filters mixed with the original makes a few soft notches that sweep up and down: a smooth, vocal swirl, gentler and more liquid than a flanger. Reach for it on synth tones, engines, sci-fi hums, force fields and tired machinery. More `stages` make more notches; `feedback` makes them sing. For a single sweep set `depth: 0` and draw `freq` with breakpoints. The output already contains the original.

freq.description: Centre of the sweep, Hz: 300 to 600 dark and throaty, 800 to 1500 classic, 2000+ airy. (100 to 5000 Hz, log scale)

depth.description: How far the sweep goes either side of `freq`, octaves: 0.5 subtle, 1.5 classic, 3+ dramatic. (0 to 4)

rate.description: Sweep speed, Hz: 0.05 to 0.3 slow and hypnotic, 0.5 to 1 classic, 2 to 6 bubbling. (0.02 to 8 Hz, log scale)

stages.description: Allpass stages; half as many notches: 2 a single gentle notch, 4 classic, 8 to 12 deep and dense.

feedback.description: Resonance, -0.95 to 0.95: 0 soft and subtle, 0.5 vocal, 0.8+ a singing whistle; negative moves the peaks between the notches. (-0.95 to 0.95)

stereo.description: Phase offset of the right channel's sweep in cycles (stereo output only): 0 the same, 0.25 swirling width, 0.5 opposite. (0 to 1)

effect-width.title: width: Width
effect-width.description: Stereo width, in stereo output only. `width` scales the difference between left and right (mid/side): 0 folds to mono, 1 leaves it, 2 is extra wide. A mono layer has no difference to widen, so give it `haas`: the right channel is delayed by a few milliseconds and the ears hear two copies, which sounds wide. The image leans toward the left (the earlier ear; pan the track a little right to centre it), and the mono sum is comb-filtered, so keep haas under about 0.015 for sounds that must also work in mono.

width.description: Side level: 0 mono, 0.5 narrower, 1 unchanged, 1.5 wider (default), 2 very wide. Breakpoints open the image up over time. (0 to 2x)

haas.description: Seconds the right channel is delayed, before the width: 0 off, 0.005 to 0.012 wide and still focused, 0.02 to 0.03 very wide (and a near-echo). (0 to 0.03 s, log scale)

effect-reverse.title: reverse: Reverse
effect-reverse.description: Plays the sound backwards: a hit becomes a swell that is sucked in and stops dead (reverse cymbals, time-rewind, ghostly inhales, sci-fi charge-ups). A track's buffer runs from its `start` to the end of the patch, silence included. By default (`align: "start"`) only the part that sounds (above -80 dB) is reversed, so the swell begins at the track's start and its climax lands one sound-length later: to hit a moment t, start the track at t minus the sound's length. `align: "end"` reverses the whole buffer, so the climax lands exactly at the end of the patch (then set `master.fadeOut` to about 0.005 so it is not faded). Pre-verb, a swell of reverb into the hit: `reverse`, `reverb`, `reverse` in one chain.

align.description: start: reverse only the part that sounds, so it begins at the track's start. end: reverse the whole buffer, so the sound finishes at the end of the patch.

effect-formant.title: formant: Formant filter
effect-formant.description: Makes any sound speak a vowel: five resonances of a voice (a, e, i, o, u) filter the input, so a saw buzz becomes a talkbox, noise a whispered vowel and a growl a creature's throat. Sweep `vowel` for talking, wah and yowling mouths ([[0, 4], [0.3, 0]] goes u-o-i-e-a); `size` scales the throat, from a tiny gremlin (0.6) to a giant (2 to 3). Richer inputs (saw, pulse, noise, drive) speak more clearly than sines. The output is matched to the input's loudness.

vowel.description: Vowel, 0 to 4: 0 a (open "ah"), 1 e, 2 i (bright "ee"), 3 o, 4 u (dark "oo"); fractions morph between neighbours. (0 to 4)

size.description: Size of the vocal tract: 1 an adult voice, 0.5 to 0.7 a child or gremlin, 1.5 a big brute, 2 to 4 a giant or monster (formants an octave or two down). (0.4 to 3x, log scale)

resonance.description: Sharpness of the formants: 1 natural, 0.5 soft and breathy, 2 to 4 ringing and whistling (synthetic, alien). (0.3 to 4x, log scale)

effect-reverb.title: reverb: Reverb
effect-reverb.description: Puts the sound in a space: early reflections and a dense, smooth tail (a 16-line feedback delay network with frequency-dependent decay). Pick a `space`, then override what you need: `decay` for length, `size` for scale, `damping` for darkness, `predelay` to keep the dry sound clear. It returns only the reverb, so on a track set `mix` to 0.15 to 0.4 (more is farther away); on a bus that several tracks send to, leave `mix` at 1.

mix.description: Wet amount, 0 to 1. Default 0.3 on a track or the master, where the dry sound passes too; on a bus (sends) every effect defaults to fully wet. (0 to 1)

space.description: The kind of space; it sets every other parameter, which you then override. room: a furnished living room. hall: a concert hall, long and lush. plate: the classic studio plate, dense and bright with no early echoes. chamber: a hard-walled echo chamber. cathedral: stone, huge, very long. cave: big, dark, irregular rock. closet: tiny and muffled. bathroom: small, bright tiles with a little flutter. car: a car interior, short and boxy. stairwell: tall concrete, ringing flutter. tunnel: long concrete tube, flutter between the walls. tank: inside a metal tank, metallic and ringing. spring: a spring reverb, the boingy chirp of guitar amps. forest: scattered reflections off trees, soft and short.

size.description: Size of the space in metres (roughly its longest dimension): spaces the echoes and the early reflections. Closet 1.4, car 2, bathroom 3, room 6, chamber 9, hall 30, cathedral 50. For spring it is the spring length (0.2 tight to 1 loose). Default: from `space`. (1 to 60 m, log scale)

decay.description: Reverb time (RT60): seconds for the tail to fall 60 dB in the mids. Car 0.15, room 0.7, hall 2.4, cathedral 6; above 10 is an endless wash. Default: from `space`. (0.1 to 10 s, log scale)

damping.description: How much faster the highs die than the mids, 0 to 1: 0 bright (tile, metal, plate), 0.5 a furnished room, 0.8 dark (curtains, carpet, forest). Default: from `space`. (0 to 1)

predelay.description: Milliseconds between the dry sound and the reverb: 0 to 5 is close to a wall, 20 to 40 separates the dry sound from a big space so it stays clear. Default: from `space`. (0 to 100 ms)

early.description: Level of the early reflections, the first echoes off the nearest walls that tell the ear the shape and size of the space: 0 none (a pure tail), 0.5 typical, 1 strong (small hard rooms, cars). Default: from `space`. (0 to 1)

diffusion.description: How smeared the echoes are, 0 to 1: low lets discrete echoes and flutter through (stairwells, tunnels), high is a smooth wash (plates, halls). Default: from `space`. (0 to 1)

width.description: Stereo width of the reverb: 0 mono, 1 natural, up to 1.5 wider than life (stereo output only). Default: from `space`. (0 to 1.5)

lowcut.description: High-pass on what enters the reverb, Hz: 150 to 300 keeps big spaces from booming and muddying. Default: from `space`. (20 to 1000 Hz, log scale)

highcut.description: Low-pass on what enters the reverb, Hz: 3000 to 6000 for a dark, distant space. Default: from `space`. (1000 to 20000 Hz, log scale)

effect-delay.title: delay: Delay
effect-delay.description: Discrete echoes: slapback off a wall, a canyon call, a dub trail. `time` (ms) sets the gap, `feedback` how many repeats, `tone` and `highpass` how each repeat darkens and thins. It returns only the echoes: set `mix` to 0.3 to 0.5 to keep the dry sound in front, or use it on a bus.

mix.description: Wet amount, 0 to 1. Default 0.35 on a track or the master, where the dry sound passes too; on a bus (sends) every effect defaults to fully wet. (0 to 1)

time.description: Milliseconds between echoes. 30 to 90 is slapback (a hard wall nearby), 150 to 400 a clear echo, 500+ a canyon. It may move: the echoes bend in pitch like a tape echo whose speed changes. (20 to 1000 ms, log scale)

feedback.description: How much of each echo comes back as the next one: 0 a single echo, 0.35 a few, 0.7 a long trail, 0.9 almost endless. Negative flips the polarity on every repeat (hollower). (0 to 0.95)

tone.description: Low-pass in the loop, Hz: every repeat gets darker. 2000 to 4000 for a tape echo, 20000 for a clean digital one. (500 to 20000 Hz, log scale)

highpass.description: High-pass in the loop, Hz: every repeat gets thinner. 300 to 800 keeps a long trail from muddying the lows. (20 to 2000 Hz, log scale)

pingpong.description: Echoes bounce between left and right (stereo output only).

modulation.description: Wobble of the echoes, cents of pitch: 5 is analog warmth, 15 to 30 a worn tape echo, 60 seasick. (0 to 30 cents)

rate.description: Speed of the wobble, Hz. (0.1 to 8 Hz, log scale)

drive.description: Saturation inside the loop, 0 to 1: each repeat comes back a little grittier and rounder, like tape. (0 to 1)

effect-resonator.title: resonator: Resonator
effect-resonator.description: Makes the input ring at chosen pitches: noise becomes a pipe or a bottle (tube), a whistle of wind through a hole (tube with a moving freq), a sympathetic string, or a metallic shimmer (metal); a click becomes a struck object. White noise comes out at about its own level; a tone at the resonance is boosted. Use `chord` for several pitches at once, and `mix` to keep some of the dry sound.

mode.description: What resonates. comb: every harmonic, buzzy and metallic-flanged. tube: odd harmonics only, hollow like a pipe, bottle or wind through a hole. string: a ringing string, warm, highs fading first. metal: inharmonic modes of a struck plate or bell, clangorous shimmer.

freq.description: Fundamental (lowest mode) in Hz. Sweep it for wind through a moving hole or a resonant whoosh; a chord adds more notes above it. (40 to 4000 Hz, log scale)

decay.description: Seconds the resonance rings after the input stops (60 dB): 0.05 a short box tone, 1 a pipe, 4+ a bell or a long metal shimmer. (0.05 to 10 s, log scale)

brightness.description: How long the upper harmonics or modes ring compared with the lowest, 0 to 1: 0 mellow and pure, 0.5 natural, 1 bright and buzzy. (0 to 1)

chord.description: More resonances, in semitones above `freq` (up to 8): [0, 7, 12] a power chord, [0, 3.86, 7.02] a just major triad, [0, 0.3] a slow beating pair.

effect-varispeed.title: varispeed: Varispeed
effect-varispeed.description: Plays the sound back at another speed, like tape or a record: pitch and length change together (use `pitch` to keep the length). Slow it for huge, heavy versions of a sound; speed it up for small, frantic ones; ramp `rate` to 0 for a tape stop, up from 0 for a spin-up. The output is longer or shorter than the input; the silence after the sound is kept for later effects. Cubic interpolation, anti-aliased when faster than 1.

rate.description: Playback speed, measured over the output time: 1 normal, 0.5 an octave down and twice as long, 2 an octave up and half as long. A ramp to 0 is a tape stop ([[0, 1], [0.6, 1], [1.4, 0]]); a ramp up from 0 a spin-up. Below a quarter speed the level falls with the speed, as a real tape or turntable does, so a stop ends in silence. (0.25 to 2x, log scale)

effect-pitch.title: pitch: Pitch shift
effect-pitch.description: Changes the pitch without changing the length (use `varispeed` for tape-style pitch and length together). Down for heavier, bigger versions of a sound; up for smaller, lighter ones; a moving `semitones` for sinking or rising pitch over a fixed sound. Granular: four overlapping grains, each aligned to the previous one so tones do not flutter; very large shifts of percussive sounds smear attacks a little.

semitones.description: Pitch shift in semitones; the length stays the same. -12 an octave down (bigger, heavier), +12 an octave up (smaller, cartoonish), 0.1 to 0.3 a subtle thickening. Breakpoints glide the pitch: [[0, 0], [1, -12]] sinks an octave over a second. (-24 to 24 st)

grain.description: Grain length in ms. 30 to 60 suits most sounds; shorter keeps hits and clicks tight but roughens low tones, longer smooths sustained tones but smears attacks into short echoes. (15 to 150 ms, log scale)

effect-doppler.title: doppler: Doppler fly-by
effect-doppler.description: Moves the sound past the listener on a straight path: the moving propagation delay bends the pitch up on the approach and down on the way out, the level follows the distance, the air dulls it far away, and in stereo it pans across with the delay between the ears. Feed it a steady sound (an engine tone, noise for a whoosh, buzzing for a bee) that lasts the whole pass. The sound arrives late by its travel time, as it does.

speed.description: Speed of the source along its straight path, metres per second: 1.5 a walker, 5 a bee, 15 a car in town, 30 on a highway, 70 a race car, 250 a jet or a bullet. It may move (a car accelerating past). (1 to 150 m/s, log scale)

distance.description: How close the path passes the listener, metres. 0.5 skims the ear (a sharp, sudden swoosh), 5 a passing car on a sidewalk, 50 a distant plane (a slow, gentle swell). (0.5 to 100 m, log scale)

time.description: When the listener hears the source at its closest, seconds from the start of the buffer. Default: the middle of the sound. (0 to 10 s)

direction.description: Which way it travels: across in front of the listener, or front-to-back (straight over the head; no panning).

amount.description: How much of the Doppler pitch bend to keep: 1 physical, 0 none (level and panning only), 2 exaggerated for cartoon fly-bys. (0 to 2)

air.description: Air absorption: highs fade with distance. 1 is physical, 3 to 6 makes distant parts much duller (haze, rain), 0 off. (0 to 4)

rolloff.description: How fast the level falls with distance: 1 physical (-6 dB per doubling), 0.5 gentler, 2 dramatic. (0 to 2)

effect-medium.title: medium: Medium
effect-medium.description: Puts the sound through a playback or transmission medium: an old TV, AM radio, telephone, walkie-talkie, megaphone, vinyl, tape, cassette or intercom, each with its band, resonances, distortion, wobble and noise. The loudness of the sound is kept; `noise` adds the medium's own hiss, hum, crackle and static around it (the walkie's only while it transmits, ending in a squelch burst). Put it last in a chain, after reverb, for a sound heard through the device.

mode.description: What the sound is heard through. tv: a 1970s CRT set, small boxy speaker, light tape wobble, faint hiss, hum and line whine. radio: AM, squashed and narrow, with static and slow fading. phone: a telephone line, 300 to 3400 Hz with digital grain. walkie: a two-way radio, narrow and crunchy, with squelch noise at the end. megaphone: a horn and an overdriven amp. vinyl: a record, crackle, warp wow and warmth. tape: reel-to-reel, saturation, head bump, gentle wow and hiss. cassette: like tape but duller, hissier and wobblier. intercom: a door or PA intercom, a cheap speaker in a metal box, with mains buzz.

amount.description: How strongly the medium colours the sound (band, resonances, distortion), 0 to 1: 1 the full character, 0.5 a cleaner set. (0 to 1)

noise.description: The medium's own noise (hiss, hum, crackle, static, squelch): 0.5 typical for the mode, 0 none, 1 heavy. (0 to 1)

wow.description: Speed wobble of media with moving parts (tv, vinyl, tape, cassette): 0.5 typical, 0 steady, 1 badly worn or warped. (0 to 1)

age.description: Wear, 0 to 1: 0 new and clean, 0.5 typical, 1 old (duller, more distorted, more crackle and dropouts). (0 to 1)

source.description: A sound source: osc, noise, fm, additive, voice, machine, chaos, modal, pluck, particles.

effect.description: An effect: filter, drive, gain, eq, compressor, limiter, transient, gate, crush, tremolo, ringmod, chorus, flanger, phaser, width, reverse, formant, reverb, delay, resonator, varispeed, pitch, doppler, medium.

event.description: One trigger of the source: seconds, or { t, pitch, vel, dur }.

repeat.description: A run of events: ratchets, bounces, rolls. accel below 1 speeds up.

interval.description: Seconds between the first two events. (0.005 to 2 s, log scale)

accel.description: Each gap is the last times this: below 1 speeds up. (0.5 to 1.5)

decay.description: dB added per repeat. (-24 to 6 dB)

pitchStep.description: Semitones added per repeat. (-12 to 12 st)

dur.description: Held length of each event, seconds. (0.001 to 5 s)

track.description: One layer: a source played by events, then its effects.

note.description: Why this layer exists, for the person tweaking it.

events.description: When the source plays. Default: once at 0. Ignored when repeat is set.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the patch. (0 to 5 s)

length.description: Cut the track after this many seconds. (0.01 to 10 s)

gain.description: Track level in dB. (-48 to 12 dB)

pan.description: Left -1 to right 1 (stereo output only). (-1 to 1)

bus.description: A shared effect chain that tracks send to.

gain.description: Bus level, dB.

master.description: The master: effects, gain, normalisation, fades.

mode.description: peak sets the highest sample, loudness the integrated loudness (LUFS).

target.description: dBFS for peak (default -1), LUFS for loudness (default -16).

ceiling.description: For loudness: the highest peak allowed, dBFS (default -0.3).

gain.description: Master level in dB, after the effects. (-24 to 24 dB)

path.description: Dot path to a parameter: tracks.body.source.freq, tracks.body.fx.space.mix, master.gain.

mode.description: set (default), mul (multiplies, breakpoints and all), add, stretch (breakpoint, envelope, event and repeat times).

from.description: Value (or factor) at the control minimum.

to.description: Value (or factor) at the control maximum.

via.description: Value at the control's default (or middle): from -> via -> to.

control.description: A knob a person sees first: a perceptual move named in the listener's words.

label.description: What the person sees: Size, Weight, Grit, Distance.

hint.description: What the listener hears across its range.

value.description: Current value between min and max; for select and toggle, the option index.

vary.description: How far variations may move it, in its own units.
